key_insight: The paper shows that large IQP-based quantum circuit Born machines can be deployed on smaller, qubit-limited hardware by injecting logical noise to break the circuit into sampleable clusters.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical inference for models that exceed current device sizes, making it easier to run large quantum generative models on near-term quantum processors.
method: Inject noise at the logical circuit level to probabilistically decompose a large IQP circuit into smaller clusters.
Sample the resulting subcircuits on qubit-limited quantum hardware and recombine the outputs.
Apply lightweight resampling on known noisy qubits to reduce the impact of introduced error.
evidence_signal: Simulations on shallow IQP QCBMs and IBM Heron experiments deploying a 316-qubit circuit onto 156-qubit hardware showed improved distribution similarity and better preservation of correlation structure.
watch_item: The approach depends on careful noise modeling and may be sensitive to hardware-specific error behavior when decomposing and resampling circuits.
paper_title: Deployment of Large IQP Circuit Born Machines on Qubit-Limited Hardware Using Noise Injection
